newsitem.title: USA: Boston Chicken sees lower 1997, '98 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Boston Chicken sees lower 1997, '98 earnings.

text.p: Boston Chicken Inc. said Wednesday its sales in the second quarter have been weak so far and that earnings for 1997 and 1998 will be hurt because it is opening fewer stores than it had originally expected.

"During this transition period, we expect store performance to be choppy and are indeed seeing sales weakness this quarter," Mark Stephens, vice-president and chief financial officer, said in a statement.
The company, which had planned to open about 300 stores a year, said it now expects to open 150 to 200 new Boston Market stores in 1997 and 150 to 250 new outlets during 1998.
The reduced targets follow the company's announcement earlier this month that it would review the pace of new store development in light of its stores' disappointing performance.
The company said the "temporary slowdown in development" will allow it to focus on making existing stores more productive.
"We are aggressively transitioning our marketing strategy to refocus on our core brand attributes ... and reining in couponing and media spending," Stephens said.
Earlier this month, the Golden, Colo.-based company announced that it would cut 115 jobs and take a 4 cent per share severance-related charge for the second quarter.

At the time, a company spokeswoman said the business was comfortable with analysts' second-quarter earnings estimates of 33 cents per share, excluding the charge, but it was not comfortable with the consensus forecast of $1.37 a share for the full year.
Boston Chicken earned $15.6 million, or 24 cents a share, on revenues of $47.3 million in the quarter ended April 21.
Boston Chicken's stock fell 18.75 cents to $15.25 on Nasdaq.
